cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and Aaron, his brother and Israel's priest (Exodus 4:14; 28:1). The Israelites are to bring them an unblemished red heifer that has no defect. I've taken picky orders before, friend, but RED, spotless AND no defect?

cards.question: The red heifer has to be unblemished with no defect. True or false: it can be a heifer that has already been put to work under a yoke.

cards.text: The heifer goes to Eleazar the priest, Aaron's son (Exodus 6:23). He has it slaughtered in his presence.

cards.question: Where does Eleazar have the red heifer brought to be slaughtered?

cards.text: Eleazar takes some of its blood on his finger and sprinkles it toward the front of the Tent of Meeting. Not once, either.

cards.question: Eleazar sprinkles the heifer's blood ___ times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.

cards.text: Then the heifer is burned in Eleazar's sight.

cards.question: When the red heifer is burned in Eleazar's sight, what parts of it go into the fire?

answers.text: Every part including its hide and dung
Only its fat and its kidneys
Only its flesh and its bones

cards.question: While the red heifer burns, the priest throws something else onto the fire. What is it?

answers.text: Cedar wood with hyssop and scarlet wool
Olive oil with frankincense and salt
Acacia wood with incense and linen

cards.text: Now everybody who worked this job cleans up. The priest washes his clothes and bathes before he comes back into the camp, and the man who burned the heifer washes and bathes too.

cards.question: The priest and the man who burned the heifer have both washed their clothes and bathed. True or false: they're still ceremonially unclean until evening.

cards.text: No amount of scrubbing changes it. It's like my oven timer. I can stare. I can pace. I can BEG. That batch is done when the timer says it's done.
Then a man who is ceremonially clean gathers up the ashes and stores them in a clean place outside the camp. Israel holds on to those ashes the way I hold on to my last bag of chocolate chips.

cards.question: The congregation keeps the heifer's ashes for preparing the water of ___.
The LORD says what the water of purification made from the heifer's ashes is for. Purification from what?
The man who gathered up the heifer's ashes was ceremonially clean when he started. True or false: he's still clean once he's gathered them.

cards.text: So he washes his clothes and stays unclean until evening, just like the other two. Three men. Three loads of laundry. ONE heifer. The LORD calls this a permanent statute for the Israelites and for the foreigner residing among them.
Now the statute turns to the people who will need those ashes. Whoever touches any dead body is unclean for seven days.

cards.question: Someone touched a dead body and is unclean for seven days. How does he become clean?

answers.text: He purifies himself with the water on the third and seventh days
He offers a lamb at the Tent of Meeting on the seventh day
He stays outside the camp for the full month after

cards.question: Someone touches a human corpse and never purifies himself. True or false: he defiles the tabernacle of the LORD.
Someone who touched a human corpse refuses to purify himself. What must happen to him?

answers.text: He must be cut off from Israel
He must pay a fine in silver
He must burn his own tent

cards.text: When someone dies in a tent, everyone who enters and everyone already inside is unclean for seven days.

cards.question: Someone has died in a tent. True or false: an open container in that tent with no lid fastened on it stays clean.

cards.text: Out in the open field, it works the same way. Touch someone killed by the sword or who died of natural causes, and that's seven days unclean.

cards.question: Out in the open field, what else makes someone unclean for seven days?

answers.text: Touching a human bone or a grave
Touching a priest's robe or sash
Touching a foreigner's cart or tent

cards.question: Here's where the stored-up ashes come in. Some go into a jar, and ___ water is poured over them.

cards.text: Then a man who is ceremonially clean dips hyssop in the water and sprinkles the tent, its furnishings and the people who were there. He sprinkles anyone who touched a bone, a grave or a person who died or was slain too.

cards.question: The clean man sprinkles the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. True or false: right after the seventh day's sprinkling, that person is clean.

cards.text: First the one being cleansed washes his clothes and bathes in water, and that evening he's clean. But if an unclean person does not purify himself, he's cut off from the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD.

The one who sprinkles the water of purification must wash his clothes, and whoever touches that water is unclean until evening. So the man getting everybody clean has some cleaning up of his own to do, like scrubbing the whole kitchen and ending up the messiest thing in it.

cards.question: One last rule: anything the unclean person touches becomes ___.

cards.text: And anyone who touches that thing is unclean until evening. That's the whole statute, friend, start to finish.
